The HTML file is not a document that opens an app: it is the app. The code, fonts and charts are all inside it, and nothing is downloaded when you use it.

Setting up: about ten minutes

  1. Extract the ZIP into a folder you will find again. A synced folder (iCloud Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, Google Drive) is ideal.
  2. Double-click MonthlyBudgetPlanner.html. It opens in Chrome, Edge, Safari or Firefox like a web page, and works offline from then on.
  3. Take the welcome tour. A few short slides on your plan, your spending, your goals and backups.
  4. Open Monthly budget and set your plan once: income, bills, subscriptions, debt payments, everyday spending and savings. Every new month starts from it.
  5. Download a backup from Settings & backup. Page 9 explains why it matters more than anything else here.

Want to look around first?

Choose Explore sample data on the welcome screen or in Settings & backup. A fictional household’s year fills every screen, in a separate session. Return to my budget brings back your own, untouched.

The idea

One honest number.

The monthly dashboard shows what’s left after your commitments: not just what’s in the account, but what’s still free once unpaid bills and planned savings are covered.

WordWhat it means
PlannedWhat you expect for the month, from your monthly budget.
ActualWhat you logged or imported.
SavingMoney moved aside: savings, sinking funds, investments. Neither income nor spending.
TransferMoney between your own accounts. Never counted.

Your plan

Plan once. It repeats.

Monthly budget holds your plan. Each new month starts from your usual amounts; change any month without touching the rest.

Groups

Income, bills, subscriptions, debt payments, everyday spending, sinking funds, savings and investments. Add or rename categories in each.

Plan tools

Use recurring amounts, Copy last month into this one, carry your opening balance, or add a category.

Budget methods

50/30/20, if you like.

Optional and off until you turn it on: Settings & backup → Budget method. Pick 50/30/20, 70/20/10, 80/20 or zero-based.

Your monthly plan gets a column per group with a bar toward its share: green within, red over, and the amount left to assign on top. Change category amounts in the plan below and the bars follow. So far compares what you’ve actually spent and saved. Open Move a line to another group to fix any category the app guessed wrong.

Day to day

Log it, or import it.

Quick log and Add transaction sit at the top of every screen. Or download a CSV from your bank and use Import CSV on Transactions.

Import CSVReads any date format, remembers the categories you pick, and skips rows you already have. PDF statements can’t be read.
Bulk actionsTick rows to change their category or delete them together, with Undo.
Recurring paymentsSet a payment once; match it when it happens with Record / match.

Keeping your budget safe.

Everything lives in your browser, on your device. Nothing is sent anywhere, there is no account, and nobody else holds a copy, including us.

Your entries live in browser storage: please read

  • Everything you enter or import is saved automatically in that browser's local storage.
  • Clearing your cache, history or site data will permanently delete it.
  • It does not carry across browsers: data added in Chrome will not appear in Safari.
  • The HTML file does not contain your entries. Copying the file does not copy your data.

Do one of these. Ideally both.

Download backup: every browser

Settings & backup → Download backup. One JSON file holding every month, category, transaction, goal, recurring payment and wealth snapshot. Restore backup brings it back on any computer. The app reminds you when a backup is due.

Daily folder backup: Chrome or Edge

Choose a synced folder once (iCloud Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, Google Drive) and a dated copy is written each day you make changes. Safari and Firefox do not offer this; use Download backup instead.

Moving to another computer

Copy the HTML file and your latest backup across, open the file, then Settings & backup → Restore backup.

When you need help

A few useful fixes.

What you seeWhat to do
It opens as code, not an appExtract the ZIP first, then right-click the file → Open with → your browser.
My numbers are goneCheck it is the same browser and profile you used before. Otherwise, Restore backup.
A payment shows twiceA card payment from checking is a transfer when the card’s purchases are already logged. Use Credit card payoff (purchases already logged).
Next month is emptyIt starts from your usual amounts. Plan tools → Use recurring amounts or Copy last month into this one.
My bank file won’t importDownload the CSV version from your bank (Download or Export), not the PDF.
I updated from an earlier versionOpen the new file in the same browser: your budget carries over. Download a backup first.
Folder backup unavailableUse Chrome or Edge on a computer, or Download backup instead.
The currency is wrongSettings & backup → Currency, or type your own symbol. Amounts are not converted.
I want the tour againSettings & backup → Welcome tour → Show tour.
